questions.question: Twice the speed of a is equal to thrice the speed of B. to travel a certain distance, A takes 42 minutes less than B to travel the same distance. What is the time (in minutes) taken by B to travel the same distance?
questions.solution:
According to the question

⇒ 2 × A = 3 × B

⇒ A : B = 3 : 2

The speed ratio of A to that of B = 3x : 2x

As we know, Time is inversely proportion to speed.

Time ratio of A to that of B = 2x : 3x

⇒ 3x – 2x = 42 min

⇒ x = 42 min

Time taken by B to complete the distance = 3 × 42 = 126 min

questions.question: A car travels at a speed of 100 km/hr and covers a particular distance in 2 hour 30 minutes. Another car travelling at the speed of 60 km/hr will cover the same distance in how much time (in hours)?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

Speed of 1st car = 100 km/hr

Time taken by 1st car = 2 hrs 30 min

Speed of 2ⁿd car = 60 km/hr

**Formula:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

2 hrs 30 min = 2 + 1/2 = 5/2

Let time taken by car to cover the distance with the speed of 60 km/hr be x hr, then

According to the question

60 × x = 100 × (5/2)

⇒ 60 × x = 250

⇒ x = 250/60

questions.question: A thief started his journey at a speed of 60 km/h. After 30 minutes, police started from the same place but at a speed of 80 km/h. How much time (in hours) will the police take to catch the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Thief's initial speed (Vt) = 60 km/h

Police's speed (Vp) = 80 km/h

Time elapsed before police starts (T) = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

**Formula:**

Distance (D) = Speed (V) × Time (T)

**Solution:**

Let the time take by police to catch the thief is t.

t = (60 km/h × 0.5)/(80 km/h - 60 km/h)

t = (30 km/h)/(20 km/h)

t = 3/2 hr

**Therefore, the police will take 3/2 hours to catch the thief.**

questions.question: Two trains A and B are 155 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 7:00 A.M. and travels towards B at 20 km/h. Another train starts from B at 8:00 A.M. and travels towards A at a speed of 25 km/h. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by **Train A** in 1 hour (from 7:00 to 8:00 A.M.) = 20 km.

Remaining distance at 8:00 A.M. = 155 − 20 = 135 km.

**Relative Speed** (opposite direction) = 20 + 25 = 45 km/h.

Time taken after 8:00 A.M. = 135 ÷ 45 = 3 hours.

Meeting time = 8:00 A.M. + 3 hours = 11:00 A.M.

**∴ The correct answer is 11:00 A.M.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance = 155 km

Speed of **Train A** = 20 km/h (Starts at 7:00 A.M.)

Speed of **Train B** = 25 km/h (Starts at 8:00 A.M.)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6365ace958fd4d5c8a78dc7875334954b8cc6feac6e24141c972893d08dfd77.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by **Train A** before **Train B** starts = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance (7 A.M. to 8 A.M.) = 20 × 1 = 20 km

⇒ Remaining distance at 8:00 A.M. = Total distance − Distance covered by A

⇒ Remaining distance = 155 − 20 = 135 km

⇒ Relative speed = Speed of A + Speed of B (since they move towards each other)

⇒ Relative speed = 20 + 25 = 45 km/h

⇒ Time taken to meet after 8:00 A.M. = Remaining distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time = 135 ÷ 45 = 3 hours

⇒ Meeting time = 8:00 A.M. + 3 hours = 11:00 A.M.

**∴ The correct answer is 11:00 A.M.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: **Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂**.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: **Sᵣₑₗ = |S₁ − S₂|**.

Time Calculation

The time required to meet is always calculated based on the distance between the objects at the **same starting time**.</p

questions.question: A policeman spots a thief from a distance of 100 metres. When he starts running after the thief, the thief starts running as well. How far will the thief have to run before being overtaken if his speed is 8 km/h and the policeman's speed is 10 km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the policeman and the thief = 100 metres

Speed of the thief = 8 km/h

Speed of the policeman = 10 km/h

**Calculation:**

Relative speed between the policeman and the thief:

Relative speed = Policeman's speed - Thief's speed

Relative speed = 10 km/h - 8 km/h = 2 km/h

Convert the relative speed to metres per second:

1 km/h = 1000 metres / 3600 seconds

Relative speed = 2 km/h = (2 × 1000) / 3600 = 5/9 metres per second

Calculate the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief:

The policeman has to cover the 100 metres gap.

Time = Distance / Relative speed

Time = 100 / (5/9) = 100 × 9 / 5 = 180 seconds

Distance run by the thief in 180 seconds:

Speed of the thief = 8 km/h = (8 × 1000) / 3600 = 20/9 metres per second

Distance run by the thief = Speed × Time = (20/9) × 180 = 400 metres

**∴ The thief will have to run 400 metres before being overtaken by the policeman.**

questions.question: The length of a train is 150 metres. In 3 seconds, it passes a man travelling at 2 km/h in the same direction as the train. Determine the train's speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 m/s.

Convert relative speed to km/h: 50 × (18 ÷ 5) = 180 km/h.

Since both are moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = Speed of Train − Speed of Man.

180 = Speed of Train − 2 ⇒ Speed of Train = 182 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 182 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the train = 150 m

Time taken to pass the man = 3 s

Speed of the man = 2 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5 ÷ 18)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52222553a3df02e418574522806da148051b7613e9d8b861bb8a83753fd7d4fa.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the train be v km/h.

⇒ Relative speed of train with respect to the man = (v − 2) km/h

⇒ Convert km/h to m/s = (v − 2) × (5 ÷ 18) m/s

⇒ Distance covered = Length of the train = 150 m

⇒ Time taken = 3 s

⇒ 150 = [(v − 2) × (5 ÷ 18)] × 3

⇒ 150 = (v − 2) × (15 ÷ 18)

⇒ 150 = (v − 2) × (5 ÷ 6)

⇒ v − 2 = 150 × (6 ÷ 5)

⇒ v − 2 = 30 × 6

⇒ v − 2 = 180

⇒ v = 180 + 2

⇒ v = 182 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 182 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Speed Conversion Rules

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed value by (5 ÷ 18). Conversely, to convert m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).
</p

questions.question: In a circular race of 1200 m, A and B start from the same point, at the same time with speeds of 27 km/h, and 45 km/h, respectively. After how much time will they meet again for the first time on the track when they running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the track = 1200 m = 1.2 km

Speed of A = 27 km/h

Speed of B = 45 km/h

**Concept:**

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds.

Time = Distance / Speed

**Solution:**

⇒ Relative speed = Speed of B - Speed of A = 45 - 27 = 18 km/h

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed = 1.2 / 18

⇒ 0.0667 hours = 0.0667 × 60 × 60 = 240 seconds

**Hence, they will meet again for the first time on the track after 240 seconds.**

questions.question: Vishnu left place A at 10 a.m. for place B, and Sudeep left place B at 2 p.m. for place A. The distance between the two places is 556 km. If Vishnu's speed is 42 km/h and Sudeep's speed is 55 km/h, then at what time will they meet each other?

questions.question: A thief steals a car at 2:00 p.m. and drives it at 70 km per hour. The theft is discovered at 3:00 p.m. and the owner sets off in another car at 105 km an hour. At what time owner will overtake the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the thief = 70 km/h

Speed of the owner = 105 km/h

Thief starts at 2:00 p.m.

Owner starts at 3:00 p.m.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Thief's head start time = 3:00 p.m. - 2:00 p.m. = 1 hour

Distance covered by the thief in 1 hour = 70 km/h × 1 h = 70 km

Relative speed of the owner compared to the thief = 105 km/h - 70 km/h = 35 km/h

Time taken by the owner to cover the distance of 70 km at a relative speed of 35 km/h:

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 70 km / 35 km/h

⇒ Time = 2 hours

Owner starts at 3:00 p.m., so the time when the owner overtakes the thief = 3:00 p.m. + 2 hours = 5:00 p.m.

**The owner will overtake the thief at 5:00 p.m.**

questions.question: Two stations A and B are 230 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 4 a.m. and travels towards B at 40 km/hr. Another train starts from B at 5 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 55 km/hr. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by **Train 1** from 4 a.m. to 5 a.m. = 40 km/hr × 1 hr = 40 km.

Remaining distance at 5 a.m. = 230 − 40 = 190 km.

**Relative speed** (opposite directions) = 40 + 55 = 95 km/hr.

Time to meet from 5 a.m. = 190 ÷ 95 = 2 hours.

Meeting time = 5 a.m. + 2 hours = 7 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd83e302b983813ce045a7a126ec7541d07e369e5fb2f103f02b2b67537170b4.png] 

**Given:**

Total distance between **Station A** and **Station B** = 230 km.

Speed of **Train A** = 40 km/hr (starts at 4 a.m.).

Speed of **Train B** = 55 km/hr (starts at 5 a.m.).

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we make the start time of both trains the same (5 a.m.).

⇒ Distance covered by **Train A** in 1 hour (from 4 to 5 a.m.) = Speed × Time = 40 × 1 = 40 km.

⇒ Remaining Distance to be covered after 5 a.m. = 230 − 40 = 190 km.

⇒ Since trains are moving in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed = SA + SB

⇒ Relative Speed = 40 + 55 = 95 km/hr.

⇒ Time taken to meet = Remaining Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 190 ÷ 95 = 2 hours.

⇒ Meeting Time = 5 a.m. + 2 hours = 7 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Same Direction Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the **difference** of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Time of Meeting

To calculate the **Meeting Time**, the distance between the objects must be considered from the point in time when both objects start moving simultaneously.</p

questions.question: A plane in flight from Mumbai to Delhi covers a distance of 1728 km in 180 minutes. What is the speed of the plane (in m/sec)?

Basic Speed Formula

Average Speed

questions.question: A 220 m long train, travelling at a speed of 99 km/h, completely crosses another train coming from the opposite direction at a speed of 81 km/h in 9 seconds. Find the length of the second train (in metres).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 99 + 81 = 180 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 180 × 5/18 = 50 m/s

Total distance (sum of lengths) = Speed × Time = 50 × 9 = 450 m

Length of second train = Total distance − First train length

Length of second train = 450 − 220 = 230 m

**∴ The correct answer is 230.**

questions.question: A, B and C run at speeds 5 m/s, 3 m/s and 8 m/s respectively. They start the race at the same time from the same point. After some time, it was found that the distance between A and C is 6 m. Determine the distance between A and B.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative speed** between **C and A** = 8 − 5 = 3 m/s.

**Relative speed** between **A and B** = 5 − 3 = 2 m/s.

Since **Time (t)** is constant, **Distance ratio** = **Relative Speed ratio**.

Distance(A−B) = [Relative Speed(A−B) ÷ Relative Speed(C−A)] × Distance(C−A) = (2 ÷ 3) × 6 = 4 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a57b3e87f4019981c361b12f4b71e3eb3aaf61d77b88d9b9247f47ced89d73be.png] 

**Given:** Speed of **A** = 5 m/s, **B** = 3 m/s, **C** = 8 m/s.

**Formula:** Distance = Speed × Time | Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₁ − S₂

⇒ Let the time be **t** seconds.

⇒ Distance covered by **C** = 8t, Distance covered by **A** = 5t.

⇒ Distance between **C and A** = 8t − 5t = 3t.

⇒ Given, 3t = 6 m ⇒ t = 2 seconds.

⇒ Distance covered by **B** = 3t = 3 × 2 = 6 m.

⇒ Distance between **A and B** = 5t − 3t = 2t.

⇒ Distance between **A and B** = 2 × 2 = 4 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (S₁ − S₂). In **opposite directions**, it is the **sum** (S₁ + S₂).

Proportionality in Motion

When **Time** is constant, **Distance** is directly proportional to **Speed** (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂). This is highly useful for race problems.</p

questions.question: Aman walks at the speed of 5 km/hr and reaches his school 28 minutes late. If he walks at 8 km/hr, then he reaches 35 minutes before the scheduled time. What is the distance of his school from his house?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:- **

Total time difference = 28 + 35 = 63 minutes = 63 ÷ 60 = 1.05 hours.

Step 2: Use the relationship between speed, distance, and time

Let the distance to the school be D km.

Time taken at 5 km/hr = D ÷ 5.

Time taken at 8 km/hr = D ÷ 8.

The difference in these times is 1.05 hours.

So,

D ÷ 5 - D ÷ 8 = 1.05.

Step 3: Solve for D

Take the LCM of 5 and 8, which is 40:

(8D - 5D) ÷ 40 = 1.05.

Simplify:

3D ÷ 40 = 1.05.

Multiply both sides by 40:

3D = 42.

Divide by 3:

D = 14.

Final Answer:

The distance to the school is 14 km.

questions.question: Two stations, A and B are 100 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 7 A.M. and travels towards B at a speed of 20 km/h. Another train starts from B at 8 A.M. and travels towards A at a speed of 25 km/h. At what time they will meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between A and B = 100 km

Speed of Train A = 20 km/h

Speed of Train B = 25 km/h

Train A starts at 7 A.M.

Train B starts at 8 A.M.

**Formula used:**

Relative speed when two trains are moving towards each other = Speed of Train A + Speed of Train B

Time taken to meet = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 20 km/h + 25 km/h = 45 km/h

Train A travels 1 hour before Train B starts, so distance covered by Train A in 1 hour = 20 km

Remaining distance = 100 km - 20 km = 80 km

Time taken to cover remaining distance at relative speed = 80 km / 45 km/h

⇒ Time = 80 / 45 hours

⇒ Time = 1.78 hours

Convert 1.78 hours into hours and minutes:

1.78 hours = 1 hour + (0.78 × 60) minutes ≈ 1 hour 47 minutes

⇒ Time ≈ 1 hour 47 minutes

Train B starts at 8 A.M., so they will meet at 8 A.M. + 1 hour 47 minutes

⇒ Meeting time = 9:47 A.M.

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**
